meta.title: Children’s literature studies today 儿童文学【高】

blocks.bodyHtml:
READING PASSAGE 3

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27–40, which are based on Reading Passage 3 below.

Children's literature studies today

Who studies children's literature and what is it that they study? The answers to this question are complex and messy, because of the many confounding factors which exist in this field.

Firstly, unlike literature for adults, children's literature is not generally written by its own readers. Adults write for children, and thus adult perceptions of what children are and of what they could and should become are woven into the literature.

Furthermore, some of those who study children's literature (and those who write certain kinds of children's books) are less interested in literary values than in the kinds of lessons it can teach- either in terms of creating better children or in terms of serving a particular curriculum. The issue of how a teacher can use a children's book is often contentious, but even outside the classroom, much material for children is still didactic.

Thirdly, while almost all literature is currently promoted within a strong commercial matrix, children's literature is often especially targeted for marketing initiatives. This fact means that readers are often recruited with a message that is negligibly literary and significantly oriented to ideas of consumption. Daniel Hade (2002) has raised useful questions about whether children's experience of reading is altered when their books are part of a larger marketing framework involving the movie, the game, and the toy of a popular children's book. How children perceive and respond to their stories in this new context is an important question.

It is also important to note that texts in an ever-increasing range of new media compete with print media for the attention of the child reader, and create definitional issues for scholars. Does the term literature' exclusively imply a verbal text? If not, where are the limits? Could a literary computer game ever be considered a work of literature? If not, what kind of attention should be paid to it, since children themselves undoubtedly perceive their print literature as part of a broader continuum? The internet provides one forum through which children now communicate with each other. (In 2003, the internet search engine Google listed 7,920,000 sites relating to the Harry Potter novels; even allowing for duplication and dead ends, that is a number with revolutionary implications.)

Finally, in the context of the higher education institutions where the formal study of children's literature is often located, at least three disciplinary frameworks (English, education, and librarianship) fragment the focus of scholarly study of children's literature.

How is the value of the imaginative encounter with the work of literature sustained and honored among such a welter of conflicting interests? One route through this maze is to ask the child readers for help. As David Lewis (2001) has perceptively noted, what children think of reading is not usually the same as what adults think, whether teachers or parents. As Lewis points out, children 'sometimes see more and they often see differently'. If those who study reading can explore children's perceptions as well as those of adults, their understanding of the nature of reading will be enhanced.

Lewis makes a further valid point when he adds that exploring children's perceptions is usually justified for educational reasons: "It is true that a better understanding of how children read and how they learn to read, is a prerequisite to improved approaches to teaching. However, it can also be argued, as Lewis rightly does, that when children's responses to literature are accessed and interpreted, they frequently lead to an understanding of how picture books appeal to children.

Young people's accounts of what and how they read also enable a more sophisticated description of many of the complex processes involved in reading. All descriptions of reading runs the risk of solipsism: i.e. this is how I read so this is what reading is for everyone. Asking other readers how they read, however, reduces that risk. For example, if I am a strong visualizer as I read, I may consider that visualization is a key component of successful reading and I may judge books by their capacity to evoke a vivid visual response. Other readers, however, may help me to realize that not everyone reads with mental pictures. Some readers respond to the patterns of the words, 'hearing' them inaudibly like a subliminal radio program. Others respond to the patterns of feelings in the story, responding with an emotional connection. Talking to competent readers, of all ages, provides a better understanding of reading experiences.

Children's insights are even more important when it comes to understanding the significance of print literature as one aspect of literary culture. Too often adults assume that reading any book at all is a more worthwhile experience than playing a digital game of any kind. A humbler approach would include asking why the game appeals to the player. Many adults will probably never develop the automatic skills to process a game as readily as they can read a book. This does not indicate that a book is better, but that a particular set of skills is absent. Non-players must acknowledge that some fictional universes are thus closed to them, and a logical response would be to find someone who can guide them to the pleasures and challenges of the gaming world. Games need to be judged individually just as books do, and any evaluative framework needs to take this into account.

meta.matchedTitle: Children's literature studies today 儿童文学

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 1
passageNotes.text: 谁在研究儿童文学、他们研究的又是什么，这两个问题本身就很复杂。作者开篇指出，这个领域之所以显得混乱，是因为有许多相互交织、彼此干扰的因素。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 2
passageNotes.text: 与成人文学不同，儿童文学通常并不是由其目标读者（儿童）创作，而是由成人写给儿童。因此，成人对“儿童是什么样的人”以及“儿童应当成为什么样的人”的看法，天然会嵌入作品内容。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 3
passageNotes.text: 不少研究者（以及部分儿童书作者）关注点并不在文学价值本身，而在作品能传递哪些“教育性教训”，例如塑造“更好的孩子”或服务某种课程目标。作者强调，即便离开课堂，很多儿童读物仍然带有明显的训诫性。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 4
passageNotes.text: 儿童文学常被纳入高度商业化的营销体系。读者接触作品时接收到的信息，往往更偏向消费导向而非文学导向。作者引用研究者提出的问题：当一本儿童书同时绑定电影、游戏、玩具等商业链条时，孩子的阅读体验是否发生了变化。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 5
passageNotes.text: 新媒体文本正不断与纸质阅读争夺儿童注意力，也让“什么算文学”变得更难界定。作者提出一系列边界问题：文学是否仅限文字文本？文学性电脑游戏是否可被归入文学？并指出儿童实际上往往把纸质阅读放在更广阔的媒介连续体中理解。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 6
passageNotes.text: 在高等教育中，儿童文学的正式研究通常分散在英语、教育学、图书馆学等至少三个学科框架里，这种学科分割进一步造成研究焦点的碎片化。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 7
passageNotes.text: 面对多重利益冲突，作者提出一条路径：直接向儿童读者请教。研究者 David Lewis 指出，儿童对阅读的看法通常不同于成人（无论教师还是家长）；儿童“有时看得更多，而且经常看得不同”。把儿童视角纳入研究，能改进我们对阅读本质的理解。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 8
passageNotes.text: Lewis 进一步认为，理解儿童如何阅读确实有助于改进教学，但价值并不限于教学技术层面。研究并解释儿童对文学的反应，常常还能帮助我们理解图画书为何会对儿童产生吸引力。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 9
passageNotes.text: 青年读者对“自己如何阅读”的描述，能帮助研究者更细致地刻画阅读过程，并降低“以己度人”的风险。作者举例说，不同读者在阅读时可能偏好不同通道：有人依靠脑内画面，有人“听见”词语节奏，有人更受情感线牵引。与不同年龄的熟练读者交流，能显著提升我们对阅读经验的理解。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 10
passageNotes.text: 在评估儿童文学与数字游戏关系时，作者反对“书天然高于游戏”的成人偏见，主张更谦逊地询问游戏为何吸引玩家。成年人读书更顺并不代表书一定更好，往往只是游戏处理技能不足。书与游戏都应当被逐项、具体地评价。

items.text:
题目：Which of the following best summarises the writer's argument in the second paragraph?
题目翻译：以下哪一项最能概括作者在第二段中的论点？
答案：A
解析：第2段明确指出“Adults write for children”，并强调成人对儿童的认知会“woven into the literature”。核心意思是儿童在作品中常以成人视角被呈现，对应 A。

题目：In the third paragraph, what does the writer say is the main interest of some people who study children's literature?
题目翻译：在第三段中，作者说某些研究儿童文学的人主要关注什么？
答案：C
解析：第3段说这类研究者“less interested in literary values than in the kinds of lessons it can teach”，即更重视作品的教化/教学功能，而非文学性本身，对应 C。

题目：The main point of the writer's argument in the fifth paragraph is to
题目翻译：作者在第五段的主要论点是要……
答案：B
解析：第5段连续提出“文学是否只限文字”“电脑游戏能否算文学”等问题，重点在讨论新媒介冲击下儿童文学边界如何变化与重划，对应 B。

questionExplanations.text:
题目 27：第二段核心是成人视角塑造儿童文学，答案 A。
题目 28：第三段强调教化功能优先于文学价值，答案 C。
题目 29：第五段讨论媒介变化对文学边界的影响，答案 B。

items.text:
题目：Children tend to make a clear distinction between print literature and electronic media.
题目翻译：儿童倾向于清楚地区分纸质文学与电子媒介。
答案：NO
解析：第5段恰恰说儿童“undoubtedly perceive their print literature as part of a broader continuum”，说明他们通常把纸媒与其他媒介放在连续体中理解，而不是清晰割裂。

题目：The study of children's literature at higher education institutions is restricted to one subject area.
题目翻译：高等教育机构中的儿童文学研究仅限于单一学科。
答案：NO
解析：第6段明确写“at least three disciplinary frameworks (English, education, and librarianship)”，显然不是单一学科，题干与原文相反。

题目：Exploring children's perceptions of reading will assist parents to choose suitable books for children.
题目翻译：研究儿童的阅读感知将帮助家长为孩子选择合适书籍。
答案：NOT GIVEN
解析：第7-8段谈到探索儿童感知可提升对阅读本质和图画书吸引机制的理解，也提到教学改进，但并未直接陈述“帮助家长选书”这一结论。

题目：Adults may appreciate the appeal of illustrated stories better, if they have more information on how children read.
题目翻译：如果成人更了解儿童如何阅读，他们可能更能理解图画故事的吸引力。
答案：YES
解析：第8段说“when children's responses ... are accessed and interpreted, they frequently lead to an understanding of how picture books appeal to children”，与题干一致。

题目：Children should be asked what features they would like digital games to include.
题目翻译：应该询问儿童希望数字游戏包含哪些功能特征。
答案：NOT GIVEN
解析：第10段主张询问“why the game appeals to the player”，即关注吸引力来源；并未提出要让儿童列出游戏应包含的具体功能。

questionExplanations.text: 题目 30-34 对应答案依次为 NO, NO, NOT GIVEN, YES, NOT GIVEN。依据分别来自第5、6、7-8、8、10段。

items.text:
题目：Young people's accounts of how they read lead to
题目翻译：年轻人关于自身阅读方式的描述会导向……
答案：F
解析：第9段指出这类描述“enable a more sophisticated description of many of the complex processes involved in reading”，即带来对阅读复杂机制更深入的认识，对应 F（a deeper knowledge of the intricacies of reading）。

题目：The risk of solipsism is reduced by
题目翻译：降低“唯我式阅读观”风险的方法是……
答案：C
解析：第9段直接说明“Asking other readers how they read ... reduces that risk”，即通过了解他人的阅读方式来避免“我怎么读，大家就怎么读”的偏差，对应 C。

题目：Strong visualisers judge books on the basis that they are
题目翻译：强视觉化读者评判书籍的依据是作品是否……
答案：H
解析：第9段举例“strong visualizer ... judge books by their capacity to evoke a vivid visual response”，对应 H（creating a variety of images in their minds）。

题目：Children's insights are important in
题目翻译：儿童视角的重要性体现在……
答案：A
解析：第10段说儿童洞见有助于理解“print literature as one aspect of literary culture”，并反对把书与游戏对立，主张在多形态文学文化中整体评估，对应 A（accepting that literature exists in a variety of forms today）。

题目：When adults read a book more easily than they play a digital game, it simply suggests
题目翻译：当成人读书比玩数字游戏更轻松时，这仅仅说明……
答案：E
解析：第10段明确写“This does not indicate that a book is better, but that a particular set of skills is absent”，即缺少某类技能，对应 E。

questionExplanations.text: 题目 35-39 答案依次为 F, C, H, A, E，证据集中在第9-10段。

items.text:
题目：What was the writer's main purpose in writing this article?
题目翻译：作者写这篇文章的主要目的是什么？
答案：C
解析：全文先梳理儿童文学研究中的多重冲突（作者、教化、商业化、媒介边界、学科分裂），再提出推进路径（纳入儿童视角、重估阅读与游戏）。主旨是“回顾挑战并提出如何前进”，对应 C。

questionExplanations.text: 题目 40：全文目的为梳理挑战并提出推进路径，答案 C。
